A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same investigation of factuality enhancement and knowledge-editing performance. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–C were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original factuality evaluations on TruthfulQA and FACTSCORE and knowledge-editing experiments using ICE and MeLLo, including numerical results in Tables 1, 3, and 4.

after.justification: v2 reports factuality and editing experiments in Tables 1–3, plus original token-distribution and hidden-state analyses in Section 5 and output cases in Appendix C.

M1.justification: v2 introduces Knowledge Token Capturing in Algorithm 1 and Section 5.1. This procedure matches tokens against contextual and parametric knowledge strings, handles shared substrings, and extracts corresponding logits and hidden states. It adds a substantive diagnostic method absent from v1.

E1.justification: TruthfulQA, FACTSCORE, and MQUAKE factual-question and editing coverage remain. v2 additionally uses MQUAKE-STUBBORN instances to examine contextual versus parametric knowledge before and after context injection. This is a limited extension within the existing knowledge-conflict domain.

E2.justification: v2 adds TruthX to the factuality, ICE, and MeLLo comparisons in Tables 1–3 while retaining DoLa, CD, ICD, and ITI. The ChatGPT/gpt-3.5 MeLLo comparison shown in v1 Figure 2 is removed.

E3.justification: v1's single-edit ICE evaluation with chain-of-thought prompting expands into comparisons using 3, 5, and 10 demonstrations and a separate 10-shot CoT condition. v2 specifies MQUAKE-CF-3K-V2, adds 13B configurations for ITI and ICD, and introduces a 2,000-instance before/after context-injection diagnostic protocol. Temperature 0.9 and top-p 0.95 are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of demonstration count and CoT, token probability and rank distributions, and hidden-state changes after context injection (Section 5, Figures 4–6). These investigate susceptibility to prompting and possible mechanisms behind editing failures. v1's two DoLa cases are replaced by a three-category error analysis and extensive additional cases in Appendix C.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 6 introduces ellipses described as 95% confidence intervals, whereas v1 provides no comparable uncertainty reporting. Their construction is not explained, and neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark accuracies.

E6.justification: The editing result sets are substantially revised: for example, 7B MeLLo baseline/ICD accuracies change from 36.8/6.9 in v1 Table 4 to 54.5/29.8 in v2 Table 3. These are reported under revised experimental settings, not established same-setting gains. v2 also adds TruthX and diagnostic findings; even retained factuality entries change, such as 13B baseline MC2 from 55.8 to 55.6.

T1.justification: v1 Section 4.1 explicitly constructs overlapping fact chains C1 and C2 and the edited chain C1'. v2 omits this general mathematical construction and retains an illustrative multi-hop example in Section 2.2. This is a limited removal of formalization; neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim shifts from impaired knowledge-editing flexibility to impaired context-faithfulness, including failures to follow contextual information and response formats. v2 qualifies factuality improvements as inconsistent and adds an explicit contribution of explaining the decline through token distributions and hidden states, rather than primarily demonstrating an editing-performance tradeoff.

C2.justification: v2 develops the overconfidence hypothesis into interpretations involving competition between contextual and parametric tokens and restricted hidden-state dispersion. It also proposes that CoT can reactivate parametric knowledge and distinguishes ignoring, denying, and misformatting context. These substantially extend v1's explanation based mainly on aggregate accuracy and two cases.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B add explicit ICE demonstrations, a MeLLo prompt template, and additional TruthX/ITI model-access information. Section 5 documents diagnostic processing, including reduction from 4096 to two dimensions with perplexity 15. Existing decoding settings and many method descriptions are retained, while v1's dataset breakdown and explicit any-of-three-questions MeLLo scoring rule are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive Related Work section and positions the study around retrieval augmentation, contextual knowledge conflicts, and the distinction between model editing and in-context editing. Newly discussed work includes Petroni et al. (2020), Si et al. (2023), Xie et al. (2024), and TruthX, substantially expanding v1's decoding-and-editing framing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around context-faithfulness. Benchmark description and evaluation are reorganized, existing individual-method descriptions move to Appendix A, and conclusion/discussion are consolidated. Author, affiliation, and publication-header text also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, restructures benchmark tables by model and prompting condition, and adds method-category symbols and red highlighting. It replaces v1's two-panel comparison with Figure 3, adds an algorithm display and diagnostic Figures 4–6, and introduces prompt and case displays. The dataset-statistics table and original case-study figure are removed.

improvement.justification: The prompting controls, systematic token/hidden-state analyses, and explicit prompts substantially strengthen v1's largely descriptive evidence and limited reproducibility. v2 also aligns its factuality discussion better with the mixed results in Table 1. Reporting problems remain: its abstract states a 69.7% maximum decline while Table 2 supports 67.9%, and the observational diagnostics do not establish causation. These limitations constrain precise quantitative and causal claims but do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
